The words of the Most High: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they can outrun Us? Evil is what they judge.﴾ We have already mentioned the verses that clarify this.

"His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat "Banī Isrā'īl," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and to parents, good treatment﴾ [al-Isrā': 23]."

And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah, he regards the trial (*fitnah*) of people as like the punishment of Allah. Its meaning is that among the people there is one who says, "We believe in Allah" with his tongue. "When he is harmed for the sake of Allah": that is, when the disbelievers inflict harm on him, as they inflict it on the Muslims, the trial of people turns him away from the religion to apostasy (*riddah*), and we seek refuge in Allah. "Like the punishment of Allah": for the punishment of Allah is a deterrent that turns one away from disbelief and sins. The meaning of "the trial of people" is the harm that he suffers from the disbelievers. The disbelievers' harming of the believers is among the kinds of testing that constitute *fitnah*, and this has been said by more than one scholar.

Accordingly, the meaning of the noble verse is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge. If good befalls him, he is content with it; but if a trial befalls him, he turns back on his face. He has lost this world and the Hereafter. That is the clear loss.﴾ [al-Hajj: 11].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if a victory comes to you from your Lord, they will surely say, "Were we not with you?"﴾. In this noble verse, the Majestic and Exalted has mentioned that the hypocrites (*munafiqun*), who say with their tongues, "We believe," while their hearts have not believed, when harm comes to the Muslims from the disbelievers while they are among them, they regard the trial of people, that is, their harm, as like the punishment of Allah. And if a victory comes from Allah to His believing servants, so that He grants them victory over the disbelievers, and they defeat them and take spoils of war (*ghana'im*) from them, those hypocrites say, "Were we not with you?" They mean that they were with the believers and among them, desiring to take their share of the spoils.

This meaning has come in other verses of the Book of Allah, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who wait for you: if a victory comes to you from Allah, they say, "Were we not with you?" And if the disbelievers get a portion, they say, "Did we not gain control over you and protect you from the believers?"﴾ [al-Nisa': 141]. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among you is he who lingers. If a disaster strikes you, he says, "Allah has blessed me, for I was not present with them as a witness." And if a bounty from Allah comes to you, he will surely say, as if there had never been any affection between you and him, "Oh, I wish I had been with them, so that I might achieve a great achievement."﴾ [al-Nisa': 72-73]. We have already presented a portion of this in surah "al-Nisa'".

Allah has made clear that they are liars in their saying, ﴿"We were with you,"﴾ and He has shown that He knows what their breasts conceal of disbelief and hypocrisy, by His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of what is in the breasts of the worlds?﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 10].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins"﴾, up to His saying: ﴿And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this, with greater clarification from the authentic Sunnah, in surah "al-Nahl" (The Bee), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge. Unquestionably, evil is what they bear﴾ [al-Nahl: 25].

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab) (Removing the Illusion of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book):

(p-363) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-'Ankabut (The Spider)

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will not bear anything of their sins at all﴾, the verse.

It is not contradicted by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens and additional burdens along with their burdens﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 13], as its explanation was previously given in full in surah "al-Nahl". Their burdens are the burdens of their misguidance, and the burdens that accompany them are the burdens of their misleading others, and that does not diminish anything of the burdens of their misguided followers.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 15:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So We saved him and the companions of the ship, and made it a sign for the worlds﴾. Its clarification has already passed in "Hud" and elsewhere.

His saying, may He be exalted, here: ﴿and made it a sign for the worlds﴾, meaning the ship of Noah, like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship. And We created for them of the like thereof that which they ride﴾ [Ya-Sin: 41-42], and similar to that of the signs.

Allah says: ﴿Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not possess for you any provision, so seek provision from Allah and worship Him.﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "al-Nahl" (The Bee), in the discussion of His words: ﴿And they worship besides Allah what does not possess for them any provision from the heavens and the earth, nor are they able﴾ [al-Nahl: 73], and in "Surat al-Furqan" (The Criterion).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 25:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And he said, "You have taken only idols instead of Allah as a bond of affection among you in the worldly life"﴾ (p-158) to His statement ﴿and you will have no helpers﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat al-A'raf, in the discussion of His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Until, when they have overtaken one another therein, the last of them will say of the first, "Our Lord, these have led us astray, so give them a double punishment from the Fire"﴾ and the verse [Al-A'raf: 38], and in Surat al-Furqan and elsewhere.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 27:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And We placed in his offspring prophethood and the Book﴾. The pronoun in His saying "his offspring" (dhurriyyatihi) refers back to Ibrahim (Abraham).

The meaning is that the prophets and messengers to whom Books were revealed after Ibrahim were all from the offspring of Ibrahim. What He mentions here about Ibrahim is mentioned in the surah "al-Hadid" (Surah 57), where Nuh (Noah) is shared with him in it. This is clear, because Ibrahim is from the offspring of Nuh, although some of the prophets are from the offspring of Nuh without Ibrahim. That is in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We had certainly sent Nuh and Ibrahim, and placed in their offspring prophethood and the Book﴾, and so on [al-Hadid: 26].

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed he is in the Hereafter among the righteous﴾. In this noble verse the Majestic and Exalted mentions that He gave Ibrahim his reward, i.e., the recompense of his deeds in this world, and that he is also in the Hereafter among the righteous.

Some scholars said: What is meant by "his reward in this world" is the good praise bestowed upon him in the abode of this world by all the people of the religions, despite their differences, whether disbelievers or believers. The good praise mentioned is "a tongue of truthfulness" (lisan sidq), in His saying: ﴿And make for me a tongue of truthfulness among the later generations﴾ [ash-Shu'ara: 84],

• and His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We made for them a tongue of truthfulness, high and exalted﴾ [Maryam: 50],

• and His saying: ﴿and indeed he is in the Hereafter among the righteous﴾. It is not hidden that righteousness in this world becomes apparent through good deeds and all other acts of obedience, and that in the Hereafter it becomes apparent through the good recompense. In this noble verse Allah has praised His prophet Ibrahim, upon him and upon our Prophet be blessings and peace. He has also praised Ibrahim in other verses;

• such as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when his Lord tested Ibrahim with words, and he fulfilled them, He said: Indeed I will make you a leader for the people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 124],

• and His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Ibrahim who fulfilled [his covenant]﴾ [an-Najm: 37],

• and His saying, the Exalted: Indeed ﴿Ibrahim was a community, devoutly obedient to Allah, upright, and he was not of the polytheists﴾ ﴿grateful for His favours; He chose him and guided him to a straight path﴾ ﴿And We gave him good in this world, and indeed he is in the Hereafter among the righteous﴾ [an-Nahl: 120–122].

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And We placed in his offspring prophethood and the Book﴾.

This noble verse indicates that prophethood and the Book are specifically in the offspring of Ibrahim, and what indicates that Nuh shares with him in this is mentioned in the surah "al-Hadid" in His saying: ﴿And We had certainly sent Nuh and Ibrahim, and placed in their offspring prophethood and the Book﴾ [al-Hadid: 26].

The answer is that the reason for restricting the mention to Ibrahim is that all the messengers after him are from his offspring, and Nuh was mentioned with him for two reasons:

The first: that everyone who was from the offspring of Ibrahim is also from the offspring of Nuh.

The second: that some of the prophets are from the offspring of Nuh and were not from the offspring of Ibrahim, such as Hud, Salih, Lut and Yunus, according to a difference of opinion regarding him. This does not contradict restricting the mention to Ibrahim, because what is meant is those who came after Ibrahim, not those who came before him or in his era, such as Lut, upon them both and upon our Prophet be blessings and peace.

Allah's saying (ta'ala): ﴿And when Our messengers came to Ibrahim with the good tidings, they said, "Indeed, we are going to destroy the people of this town..."﴾ (the verse). We have already explained it in Surah Hud, in the discussion of His saying (ta'ala): ﴿And when the good tidings came to him, he began to argue with Us concerning the people of Lut﴾ [Hud: 74].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 33:

Regarding His saying, ﴿And when Our messengers came to Lot﴾, up to His saying: ﴿for a people who reason﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this, along with some supporting evidence, in Surah "Hud" in the discussion of the story of Lot, and in Surah "al-Hijr".

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And to Midian [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb﴾, up to His words: ﴿lying prostrate in their homes﴾. Its explanation has already been given in Surat al-A'raf, in the discussion of his story with his people, and also in ash-Shu'ara'.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 38:**

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And [We destroyed] 'Ad and Thamud, and it has become clear to you from their dwellings. Shaytan made their deeds appear fair to them and barred them from the way, though they were discerning.﴾ ﴿And Qarun, Pharaoh and Haman. Musa had certainly come to them with clear proofs, but they acted arrogantly in the land, and they were not ones who could escape.﴾ ﴿So each We seized for his sin. Among them were those upon whom We sent a violent wind, and among them were those seized by the Blast, and among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow, and among them were those whom We drowned.﴾

The apparent reading is that his saying "and 'Ad" is the object of an implied verb, "We destroyed" (ahlakna). This is indicated by his preceding saying: ﴿So the earthquake seized them﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 37], meaning: We destroyed Madyan with the earthquake, and We destroyed 'Ad. What supports this mentioned destruction is his following saying: ﴿and it has become clear to you from their dwellings﴾, meaning: those dwellings are empty of them because of their destruction. Also his further saying after it: ﴿So each We seized for his sin.﴾

In these noble verses, the Exalted has pointed to the destruction of 'Ad, Thamud, Qarun, Pharaoh and Haman. Then He declared that He seized each of them for his sin. Then He detailed, in the manner of what is called in rhetoric (badi') the *laff wa-l-nashr al-murattab* (an arrangement that lists items and then matches each with its corresponding explanation in order), the causes of their destruction, saying: ﴿Among them were those upon whom We sent a violent wind﴾ (p. 160) — and this is *al-ha:sib* (the violent wind), meaning 'Ad. The evidence is His saying: ﴿As for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind﴾ [al-Haqqah: 6], and His saying: ﴿And in 'Ad, when We sent upon them the barren wind﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 41], and similar verses.

His saying: ﴿and among them were those seized by the Blast﴾ means Thamud, by the evidence of His saying concerning them: ﴿And the Blast seized those who did wrong, so they became prostrate in their homes, as if they had never lived there. Unquestionably, Thamud disbelieved in their Lord. Unquestionably, away with Thamud!﴾ [Hud: 67–68].

His saying: ﴿and among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow﴾ means Qarun, by the evidence of His saying concerning him: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾ — the verse [al-Qasas: 81].

His saying: ﴿and among them were those whom We drowned﴾ means Pharaoh and Haman, by the evidence of His saying: ﴿Then We drowned the others﴾ [al-Saffat: 82], and similar verses.

The more evident reading of His saying in this verse: ﴿and they were discerning﴾ is that their discernment mentioned here refers only to the life of this world, as indicated by His saying: ﴿They know an outward aspect of the life of this world, but of the Hereafter they are heedless﴾ [al-Rum: 7], and His saying: ﴿And they will say: "Had we listened or reasoned, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze"﴾ [al-Mulk: 10], and similar verses. His saying: ﴿and they were not ones who could escape﴾ is like His saying: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they will outrun Us? Wretched is their judgment﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 4].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 41:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The parable of those who take protectors other than Allah is like the spider, which takes a house; and indeed, the frailest of houses is the spider's house, if only they knew.﴾ ﴿Indeed, Allah knows whatever they invoke besides Him of anything; and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ ﴿And these parables We present to the people, but none understands them except those of knowledge.﴾

We have already mentioned the verses that clarify this in surah "al-A'raf," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So his likeness is like the likeness of the dog﴾ [al-A'raf: 176], the verse, and in other places.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 45:

Allah's statement: ﴿Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "al-Kahf," in the discussion of His statement: ﴿And recite what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord; none can alter His words﴾ [al-Kahf: 27].

Allah's statement: ﴿And establish the prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing﴾.

(p-161) We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "al-Baqarah," in the discussion of His statement: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 45].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 46:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in a manner that is best, except for those of them who have committed wrong﴾.

We have already presented its explanation, and the explanation of ﴿except for those of them who have committed wrong﴾ was given at the end of Surah an-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And argue with them in a manner that is best﴾ [an-Nahl: 125].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 51:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book, which is recited to them? Indeed, in that is mercy and a reminder for a people who believe.﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in the beginning of Surat "al-Kahf" and at the end of Surat "Ta-Ha," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Has there not come to them clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures?﴾ [Ta-Ha: 133], and elsewhere.

The Words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and were it not for a specified term, the punishment would have come upon them. And it will surely come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive.﴾ ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and indeed Hell is encompassing of the disbelievers.﴾ We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah al-An'am, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿What I have is not what you are asking to hasten.﴾ [al-An'am: 57], and in Surah Yunus, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Then when it occurs, will you believe in it? Now? And you had been [once] asking to hasten it.﴾ [Yunus: 51], and in Surah ar-Ra'd, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the evil before the good...﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 6].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 56:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is spacious, so worship Me alone﴾. Allah, exalted and majestic is He, addressed His believing servants, affirmed to them that His earth is spacious, and commanded them to worship Him alone, to the exclusion of others, as indicated by the fronting of the object, which is "iyyaya" (Me alone), as we explained in the discussion of His saying: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5].

The meaning is: if they are in a land where they cannot establish their religion, or where the harm of the disbelievers reaches them, then indeed the earth of their Lord is spacious, so let them emigrate to a place within it where they can establish their religion and be safe from the harm of the disbelievers, just as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims did.

(p-162) This meaning indicated by this noble verse also occurs in other verses, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves, the angels will say, "In what [condition] were you?" They will say, "We were oppressed in the land." The angels will say, "Was not the earth of Allah spacious that you could emigrate therein?"﴾ [an-Nisa': 97], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the earth of Allah is spacious. Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account﴾ [az-Zumar: 10].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 57:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Every soul shall taste death﴾ [al-Ankabut: 57]. Its meaning has come clarified in other verses;

• such as His saying, may He be exalted, in the surah of "Al 'Imran": ﴿Every soul shall taste death. And you will only be given your full reward on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Al 'Imran: 185],

• and His saying: ﴿Everyone upon it will perish﴾ [al-Rahman: 26],

• and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Everything will perish except His Face﴾ [al-Qasas: 88].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 58:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely settle them in lofty chambers within Paradise﴾.

We have already presented the meaning of ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, clarified at the beginning of Surat al-Kahf. We have also presented the meaning of "We will surely settle them" (lanubawwi'annahum) in Surat al-Hajj, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [mention] when We settled for Abraham the site of the House﴾. And we have mentioned the verses in which the "chambers" (al-ghuraf) are mentioned at the end of Surat al-Furqan, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those will be rewarded with the chamber﴾ and the verse [al-Furqan: 75].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 60:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And how many a creature there is that does not carry its provision; Allah provides for it﴾.

In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that many of the creatures (dawabb) that cannot carry their provision because of their weakness, it is He, majestic and exalted, who provides for them. He clarified this meaning in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that upon Allah is its provision, and He knows its place of dwelling and its place of storage. All is in a clear register﴾ [Hud: 6].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 61:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?"﴾ up to His saying ﴿Say, "Praise be to Allah." But most of them do not reason.﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this matter in the utmost clarity in Surah "Banu Isra'il" (Surah al-Isra'), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright﴾ [al-Isra' 17:9].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 65:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when they board the ship, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to the land, at once they associate others with Him.﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "Bani Isra'il," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish except Him﴾, up to His saying: ﴿a pursuer﴾ [al-Isra' 67–69], and in other places.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have they not seen that We have made [it] a secure sanctuary, while people are being snatched away from all around them?﴾ and so on.

In this noble verse, Allah, Mighty and Exalted, reminds the Quraysh of His favour upon them, that He made for them a secure sanctuary, meaning the Sacred Precinct of Makkah (Haram Makkah). They are safe within it regarding their wealth and their lives, while people outside the Sanctuary are seized, killed and taken captive.

This meaning indicated by this noble verse is explained in other verses:

• His saying, may He be exalted, in [Surat] al-Qasas: ﴿They said, "If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land." Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary?﴾ and so on [al-Ma'idah: 97],

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever enters it is safe﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 97],

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a means of stability for the people﴾ and so on [al-Ma'idah: 97],

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House, who has fed them against hunger and secured them against fear﴾ [Quraysh: 3–4].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 29, verse 69:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And those who strive in Our cause — We will surely guide them to Our paths.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, mentions that those who strive in His cause, He will guide them to the paths of goodness and right guidance. He swore to this, as indicated by the lam of emphasis in His words: "lanahdiyannahum" (surely We will guide them).

This meaning is clarified in other verses, such as the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And those who were guided — He increases them in guidance﴾ [Muhammad: 17], and His words: ﴿As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith﴾ [at-Tawbah: 124], as its explanation has already passed.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with the doers of good.﴾

We have already explained this at the end of Surah an-Nahl, in the discussion of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good﴾ [an-Nahl: 128].
